title: Understand Costs and Choose Budgeting and Support
objective: Understand the relationship between usage and pricing, and explain cost allocation, budget notifications, pricing estimates, and support plans based on business requirements.

sections.title: Turn Usage Facts into Actionable Cost Information
paragraphs: The first step in billing is not checking the bill at the end of the month, but creating a state in which you can understand what each team, application, and environment is using. AWS Billing and Cost Management provides features that help analyze, organize, plan, and optimize costs.

When multiple teams use the same AWS environment, apply consistent tags to resources, enable cost allocation tags in billing management, and then track costs by team, application, environment, or other relevant unit. Cost categories provide a way to map multiple expenses to business classifications. The goal is not tagging itself, but enabling the people responsible for the expenses to verify why resources are being used and decide on improvements.

With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, the management account tracks the total costs of member accounts in the organization and is responsible for paying the bill. Consolidated billing does not automatically combine the credentials or ordinary resource permissions of each member account. AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes incurred costs and usage. When a person responsible for costs finds an increase, they make a decision only after checking the affected service, usage volume, tags, and business necessity.

sources.label: Organizing and Tracking Costs Using Cost Allocation Tags

sections.title: Connecting estimates, budgets, and actuals
paragraphs: Before implementation, enter the planned services and usage amounts in AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate costs. After operations begin, use AWS Cost Explorer to review costs and usage by service. If costs are higher than estimated, investigate whether any services are being used more than expected.

AWS Budgets can notify you when actual or forecast spending or usage exceeds a configured threshold. For example, if you configure notifications at 80% of the monthly budget, you can begin investigating before the budget is fully used.

When setting a budget, also decide who will receive notifications, the deadline for reviewing them, and who is responsible for deciding how to respond. If a budget action will stop the target resources, first confirm the impact on users and the approval process.

sections.title: Choose a pricing model based on acceptable usage variability and interruption tolerance
paragraphs: When choosing a pricing option, consider how far you can forecast usage, whether the workload can tolerate interruptions, and how much flexibility you need to change the configuration. On-Demand requires no advance commitment to a term or usage amount. With Savings Plans, committing to a fixed hourly spend for a term gives you lower rates on eligible usage. Consider Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances if you expect to use an eligible configuration for a set term. A Regional Reserved Instance discounts eligible usage in that Region. A Zonal Reserved Instance also reserves capacity for matching EC2 instances in the specified Availability Zone.

Spot Instances are a low-cost option for workloads that can tolerate interruptions or relocation and use surplus capacity. Compare Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances when hardware dedication or licensing requirements apply. Also consider Capacity Reservations, storage class and retention period, inbound and outbound data transfer, and inter-Region data transfer together with the workload requirements. Long-term usage does not always mean that the same purchasing option should be selected.

AWS Budgets can also track Savings Plans utilization and coverage. Those considering discounts should identify stable baseline usage and separate out uncertain demand by keeping it under a flexible pricing model. Always confirm the latest prices, eligible services, and conditions in the official pricing information.

sources.label: Regional and Zonal EC2 Reserved Instances

sections.title: Choosing Support and Recommendations by Role
paragraphs: Choose a support plan based on the types of assistance your organization needs and its expectations for response times. Basic Support provides access to account and billing questions, service quota increases, documentation, and more; higher-tier plans expand the scope of technical support. Because plan names and response terms may change, check the latest official information when entering into an agreement.

AWS Trusted Advisor provides checks and recommendations related to cost optimization, security, performance, fault tolerance, service quotas, and more. The checks available depend on the support plan. Use the AWS Health Dashboard to check the status of AWS services and events that may affect your account. Neither tool automatically makes configuration changes or decisions on your behalf.

When researching technical information, use AWS official documentation, whitepapers, the Knowledge Center, re:Post, and other resources according to your purpose. AWS Marketplace provides access to third-party products, but before adopting one, verify its functionality, pricing, security, and operational responsibilities.

sources.label: CLF-C02 Domain 4: Technology Resources and Support

checkpoints.prompt: The finance manager for a new project wants to receive a notification based on actual or forecast spending when the project's monthly cloud costs approach 80% of the budget, and then ask the responsible team to verify them. Which AWS feature is most appropriate?

choices.text: Register the monthly budget in AWS Budgets and notify the responsible personnel when the threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: AWS Budgets can send notifications when actual or forecast spending exceeds a threshold. Set 80% of the monthly budget as the threshold and configure notifications for both actual and forecast spending.

choices.text: Use only AWS Cost Explorer to configure threshold notifications for forecast future spending.
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes incurred costs and usage. Use AWS Budgets for threshold notifications that include forecasts.

choices.text: Send daily notifications treating the pre-launch estimate from the pricing calculator as actual costs.
choices.explanation: The pricing calculator provides an estimate based on assumptions made before launch; it is not used to notify you about actual or forecast spending incurred during operation.

choices.text: Check Cost Explorer at the end of the month without configuring a threshold or notifications.
choices.explanation: Analyzing costs at the end of the month with Cost Explorer is useful, but it does not meet the requirement to notify the responsible personnel when spending approaches the budget.

checkpoints.prompt: Several business divisions use a single AWS organization. A corporate planning manager wants to analyze monthly costs by application and environment and review them with the respective owners. Which preparation is most appropriate?

choices.text: Apply consistent tags to resources, activate the tags as cost allocation tags in Billing, and organize the data with cost categories and Cost Explorer as needed.
choices.explanation: Tags must not only be applied; they must also be activated as cost allocation tags in Billing. With consolidated billing in Organizations, the management account can track total costs and analyze them by account, application, and environment using cost categories and Cost Explorer.

choices.text: Tag the resources, but analyze the costs without activating the tags as cost allocation tags in Billing.
choices.explanation: User-defined tags must not only be applied; they must be activated as cost allocation tags in Billing before they appear in Cost Explorer and other tools.

choices.text: Assume that using consolidated billing in Organizations automatically classifies costs by business division without configuring tags or cost categories.
choices.explanation: Consolidated billing tracks the organization's total costs and bills the management account, but it does not automatically determine business classifications.

choices.text: Assume that because each member account is independent, the management account cannot track costs for the organization as a whole.
choices.explanation: Although member accounts normally have independent permissions, consolidated billing enables the management account to track the total costs within the organization.

checkpoints.prompt: A team operating a production order service is looking for a support plan that allows it to consult AWS for technical assistance during incidents. Select the one most appropriate item to confirm before signing the contract.

choices.text: Confirm the scope of technical support required and response-time expectations, then compare the plans using the latest official plan information.
choices.explanation: Basic supports questions about accounts and billing, service quota increase requests, and similar matters, while higher-tier plans offer broader technical support. Compare the plans based on the support the business needs and the current official terms.

choices.text: Assume that the same technical support is available with every plan.
choices.explanation: The technical support available with Basic Support differs from that available with other plans.

choices.text: Choosing a support plan eliminates the need for the customer to manage access controls and monitoring.
choices.explanation: Support does not replace the customer's security configurations or operational responsibilities.

choices.text: Look only at past pricing tables and do not verify the current service terms.
choices.explanation: Pricing and plan terms may change, so the current official information must be verified before signing the contract.
